title: Draft: extcap: Improved debug log handling
description:
Issue:
When --debug or --debug --debug-file is used, no logging is produced.
It is required to use --log-level=debug in addition to it, but when
used, output is written to requested file and to console (STDERR) too.
Output to console confuses wireshark/tshark then.

Changes:
When --debug used, log level is set to debug automatically.
If --debug-file used, log to console is disabled (discarded).
Change involves any application based on extcap/extcap-base.c.

notes.body: Is there a reason to add a new `wslog_set_writer()` interface instead of using the existing `wslog_init_with_writer()`?
Yes. The change must set writer much later than wslog_init_with_writer() is called. So I think that new API call is needed.
Why does it have to be later?
Because the need of setting writer is derived on parameters (when --debug-level is issued). It happens much later than log is initiated by wslog_init().
OK, understood. I see now that extcaps were implemented to change the log handler mid-flight.

@rknall, @crondaemon: There is change I proposed.

Usecase without the change:
1. Start wireshark (or use tshark) and try randpkt, enable debug and choose log name. Run capture.
2. It shows generated packets, but log file is empty.

=> Debug can't be enabled.

Triggering the issue without the change:
1. set export WIRESHARK_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
2. Repeat scenario above

=> Wireshark/tshark gets confused. Debug file is not empty.

With change first scenario works fine - wireshark/tshark works fine and debug file contains expected information.

I'm sorry, I got lost. Scenario one above is solved with this MR. So I'm afraid that !5311 is redundant and when it will be merged, it will probably cause merge conflict with this MR. But if you think !5311 is useful, lets do it.

My goals are:
--debug will start logging at DEBUG level to console
If --debug-file is used, logging will be routed to file only, no output to console.

Did I missed something?

!5311 is bug-for-bug how extcap logging was working before wslog was introduced.

And IMHO a cleaner change to the wslog.h API, and avoids an empty log handler, which to me is a hint that something is amiss in the design.

I took the liberty of fixing the bug you reported from a clean slate. If you don't mind rebasing your changes on top of !5311, I would really appreciate that.

The bug reported and fixed in !5311 is that the extcap log file is always empty. New behaviour like writing debug output to stderr is not included in that change (intentionally).

The log file bug was introduced in dc7f0b88bba0c703d9c802b153e145dc6b3dc549. That commit also added debug logging to the console, but it was done in a broken incomplete way, so that is also removed.

That's why I said !5311 brings the feature level bug-for-bug what it was before wslog.
OK. Merge it and I will rebase to new master...
Merged !5311. Thanks for your cooperation. I created issue #17764 to track the second bug you reported.

I believe it is ready for merge.
I think this should be fixed, not turned into documented behavior.
I don't think this is true for current master.

Note: --log-level and other hidden parameters are evaluated by all Wireshark applications. You removed its parsing by removing `ws_log_parse_args(&argc, argv, NULL, LOG_ARGS_NOEXIT);`. I put it back with my patch, but nevertheless environment variables are evaluated either.

I think it is true. Lets try:

`WIRESHARK_LOG_LEVEL=debug ./run/wireshark and run e.g. randpkt`

Wireshark will show a lot of errors as it receives debug output as part of generated packets. It took me hours than I recognized what is behind. BTW when --debug didn't worked, it was the only way how to debug extcap...

So I documented this consequences for future.

This was fixed in e921b804d0174b2bb5a118df8b454c0dc2e69369.

I tried the lastest master exactly as you described and I get no errors running randpkt.

I did remove the `ws_log_parse_args()` call, because when extcaps are launched as child processes this call serves no purpose.
By the way I'm not sure if you are aware of this, it's easy to miss, but WIRESHARK_LOG_LEVEL is used with `ws_log_init()`, not `ws_log_parse_args()`.
Yes, my mistake. I added ws_log_parse_args() back to behave as any other Wireshark tool. But we can remove it if you wish (and remove reference from documentation).

If it's useful to have `ws_log_parse_args()` to run from the CLI I'm fine with keeping it. You might want to consider moving that call to `extcap_log_init()` to remove the code duplication (obviously you will have to add argv/argc as arguments).

Did you confirm that randpkt runs fine with `WIRESHARK_LOG_LEVEL=debug` after e921b804d0174b2bb5a118df8b454c0dc2e69369 and that that bug is now fixed?

This will write debug messages to stderr so it will confuse Wireshark and break extcaps with debug enabled without a log file.

Putting a warning in the documentation against it is not a proper fix IMO.
As I wrote above - there should be option how to print debug to console. User just must have a way how to avoid it (sequence of `--debug --debug-file=`). To make it clear, I documented it.

I honestly don't get what your are trying to achieve here. This creates new issues and it doesn't even solve what you were trying to do in the first place, which is write debug messages to the console.

What am I missing?

I hope I explained it above.

Another solution is to create something like --debug=cli and --debug=wireshark and first option will just enable debug and second will enable debug and will route output somewhere. But to where in this case.

So I think it is more clear to use --debug and --debug-file and explain how to use it.
Aren't extcaps meant to be launched by the GUI? Is there a use case for using the CLI, other than the most basic testing of extcaps?
By GUI I mean wireshark and tshark. I'm not sure I understand what use case you have in mind.

Yes, extcaps are destined to start by GUI, but they can be run alone and for developers it is MUST to be able to run them alone and be able to troubleshoot.

During development you run it 99% from CLI because there is nearly no need of GUI. Output (packets) are written to file, not to STDOUT so you can check it later. And you type, compile, run and run Wireshark over and over is slower than just run extcap.

I see, thanks for explaining it.

Still your patch breaks running an extcap with --debug from the GUI (without --debug-file) so it needs additional work.
Can you check if !5322 does what you need?

+== DEBUG LOGGING
+
+--debug::
++
+--
+Enables debug and sets logging level to debug. If used alone, output is sent to STDERR.
+--
+
+--debug-file=<path to file>::
++
+--
+File where log output will be written. When used, output is written to the file only and no output is sent to STDERR. It works even no *--debug* is used.
+--
+
+When extcap program is called from wireshark or tshark and debug is enabled, it will confuse them. *--debug-file* must be used to avoid it!

+Do not use hidden parameter *--log-level=* nor other hidden *--log-...* parameters with extcaps when run from wireshark/tshark. Do not use *WIRESHARK_LOG_...* variables too. It routes some messages to STDERR and it confuses calling application.
